fields.h1: Build a Wedding Photography Contract Couples Sign Online
fields.hero_description: Build a wedding photography contract that fills in each couple's package, sets payment due dates, and collects every signature.
fields.features_heading: Every Booking Term in One Signed Contract
fields.features_subheading: The couple makes one choice and signs. Everything between those two steps is built from your packages and your terms.
fields.feature_1:
Packages that fill in the coverage terms

The couple picks one of your packages, and its hours, price, and inclusions fill the coverage section of the contract. Change a price once and every new contract quotes it.
fields.feature_2:
Payment dates set by the wedding date

Set the retainer as a share of the package and the balance as a number of days before the wedding. The contract states both amounts in dollars, each with the date it is due.
fields.feature_3:
Clauses that show up only when they apply

A travel clause joins the contract when the venue is past your mileage limit, and an overtime rate joins when the couple adds hours. Couples read only the terms that fit them.
fields.feature_4:
Signatures from both partners, then yours

The last screen captures an e-signature from each partner, then from you. The contract is marked signed only when every signature is in, and each one is saved with its date.
fields.feature_5:
A reminder before the balance comes due

The couple gets an email 14 days before the balance date. If the date passes and nobody has marked the balance paid, you get a Slack alert that links to the contract.
fields.feature_6:
The full code, exported to GitHub

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Your contract form can then sit beside your studio website's code, where a developer can review any change first.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Bookings and the Contract Each Needs
fields.tab_content_1:
Full Day, with $1,050 now and $3,150 by May 13

Tessa Brightwater and Omar Haddad pick the 8-hour Full Day package from Juniper Hollow Photography, priced at $4,200. The contract fills in a $1,050 retainer due at signing and a $3,150 balance due May 13, ahead of their wedding on June 12, 2027. Both of them sign on the last screen, then the photographer signs.
fields.tab_content_2:
Past 100 miles, your contract adds a $600 travel fee

Bramblewood Studio covers venues within 100 miles at the package price. Nadia Petrov and Callum Reyes book a vineyard 140 miles away, and their contract adds a travel clause: a $600 travel fee plus 1 hotel night that the couple books. This month's other 3 bookings sit under the limit and carry no travel terms.
fields.tab_content_3:
With one of two signatures in, October 9 waits

Delphine Okafor and Rhys Calder move their wedding with Larkfield Photo from September 18 to October 9. The app drafts an amendment that sets the new date and carries their $900 retainer over to it. Delphine has signed, and one of two signatures is in. The photographer gets a Slack message the moment Rhys signs.
fields.tab_content_4:
For $450, Kofi signs over copyright and posts 20 images

Mireille Santos of Copper Fern Studio hires Kofi Boateng to second-shoot a Saturday wedding at a $450 day rate. His contract transfers copyright in his images to the studio in writing and lets him post 20 of them once the couple has their gallery. He signs on his phone, and the signed copy joins the studio's contract table.

fields.howto_title: How to Create Your Wedding Contract
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a wedding photography contract that fills in each booking's terms, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Gather the clauses you already use
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each package you sell and what it costs, plus the add-ons a couple can choose, such as an extra hour or an engagement session. These become the choices on the form and the prices the contract quotes back to the couple.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Collect the clause wording you stand behind, starting with cancellation and image delivery. If a lawyer drafted your current contract, keep that wording exactly as written and paste it into your prompt clause by clause, each under a plain heading.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Tell Emergent which fields the couple fills in, how the retainer and balance are worked out, and when each optional clause appears. Emergent builds the form, the contract page couples read, and a database table with one row per booking.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Open a sample contract for your largest package and do the sums by hand. The retainer and the balance should add up to the package price, and the balance date should fall as many days before the wedding as your terms set.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Decide where each signed copy goes
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose what happens once the last signature is in: a copy emailed to the couple, a Slack message to you with the wedding date in it, and the booking marked signed in your table. Keep that message short enough to read on a phone.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it with a made-up booking
fields.howto_step_6_des: Book a fake wedding past your mileage limit with an extra hour added, and sign as both partners. The travel clause and the overtime rate should both appear, and the balance date should match your terms. Fix anything that is off by prompting.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the form on a custom domain; Emergent includes custom domains, and they use credits. Send the link when a couple says yes, and retire your old PDF contract so nobody signs two versions of the same terms.

faq_plan.q: What is a wedding photography contract?
faq_plan.a: It is the signed agreement between a wedding photographer and the couple that sets what the photographer covers on the day and what the couple pays. It names the date, the venue, the hours, the price and its payment dates, and what happens if either side cancels or the date moves.

faq_plan.q: How to make a wedding photography contract?
faq_plan.ref: how to make a wedding photography contract
faq_plan.a: List your packages and the clauses you already trust, then describe the contract to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English. Emergent builds the form each couple completes and signs, with your prices and payment dates worked into the terms. Run one fake booking through it before a real couple gets the link.

faq_plan.q: What should a wedding photography contract include?
faq_plan.ref: What should a wedding photography contract include?

prov.original: What should a wedding photography contract include?

faq_plan.a: It should include both parties' names, the wedding date and venue, the hours of coverage, and the price with its retainer and balance dates. Add the number of edited images and when they arrive, the cancellation and date-change terms, and the couple's rights to use the photos. Under US law, copyright vests initially in the photographer who took them.

faq_plan.q: Why do I need a wedding photography contract?
faq_plan.ref: why do i need a wedding photography contract
faq_plan.a: You need one because it fixes the price and the cancellation terms in writing before either side spends money. If the date moves or the gallery runs late, both of you can point to the clause you signed. Keep planning details out of it: a client onboarding questionnaire collects those once the booking is signed.

faq_plan.q: Who signs the wedding photography contract?
faq_plan.ref: who signs the wedding photography contract
faq_plan.a: The photographer, or whoever signs for the studio, and the clients paying for the coverage. Name both partners as clients and have each one sign; the contract should not rest on one partner's signature. If a parent pays part of the fee, add them as a signer too, with the amount they cover.

faq_plan.q: What does a wedding photography package include?
faq_plan.a: Each package sets the hours of coverage, the number of photographers, and what the couple receives afterward, such as an online gallery or an album. Copy every package into the contract word for word. The hours the couple signs for should match the hours you plan to shoot.

faq_plan.q: How to write a wedding photography contract?
faq_plan.ref: how to write a wedding photography contract
faq_plan.a: Write it in plain sentences, one clause per topic, in the order a couple reads it: coverage, money, delivery, changes, then rights. Use one name for each thing throughout, and state every amount and deadline as a number. Have a lawyer licensed in your state review the final text before any couple signs it.

faq_plan.q: How many pictures are in a standard wedding photography contract?
faq_plan.ref: how many pictures the standard wedding photography contract
faq_plan.a: There is no standard number; each contract sets its own. Write a minimum or a range of edited images you can deliver at your hardest wedding, and tie it to the hours of coverage. Count only edited images toward it, since outtakes stay out of the total.

faq_plan.q: How much is a wedding photography contract?
faq_plan.ref: how much is wedding photography contract
faq_plan.a: Writing your own costs nothing but time, and a lawyer's review is billed at their hourly or flat rate. Putting it online for couples to sign costs nothing to start either: Emergent is free to start, and its free tier covers building and publishing the contract form.

faq_plan.q: How to cancel a wedding photography contract?
faq_plan.ref: how to cancel a wedding photography contract
faq_plan.a: Follow the cancellation clause in the contract you signed. Send notice the way it says, in writing if it asks for writing, and keep a dated copy. Read what it says about the retainer: if the contract calls it nonrefundable, expect to lose it. Photographers who build their contract on Emergent keep every signed copy in a database they own, with the exact terms each couple agreed to.

plan.angle: The top 10 is photographer blogs and forum threads listing clauses, plus template sellers (Lightfolio, esign.com, an Etsy listing); none turns the contract into something the couple fills in and signs with their own package, money dates and venue already worked into the terms. This page is for the photographer who books on contract: the package picked sets hours and price, the retainer and balance dates come from the wedding date, travel and second-shooter terms appear only when they apply, every signer signs on screen, and each signed booking is a row in a database the photographer owns. The FAQ answers the clause, signer, cost and cancellation searches as plain advice, with the copyright point sourced to the statute, and makes no claim that the form makes a contract enforceable.

truth.evidence: Copyright lines match the 17 U.S.C. 201(a)/204(a) quotes ('vests initially in the author', 'in writing and signed'); Emergent lines map to prompt-build, e-signature-capture, alerts, database-owned, no-caps, code-export, free-start, custom-domain; 1,050 + 3,150 = 4,200 and May 13 is 30 days before June 12, matching the mockup's '30 days before the wedding'.
